reason: Excluded on resource grounds by explicit user decision. The base CurveCurator run reached only ~11% of curve fitting (277 of 2432 batches) after 18.5 minutes, with tqdm projecting ~2h51m remaining. The container has 4 logical CPUs while three executors ran concurrently requesting 5 (decryptM), 2 (kinobeads) and 5 (viability) cores respectively, i.e. ~12 CPU-bound workers on 4 cores, driving the load average to ~47; the smallest example in the set (155 KiB) consequently took 948s. The coordinator presented the options (continue, exclude, or restart serially) and the user chose to exclude this example and proceed with the two smaller ones. The pipeline processes were terminated with SIGTERM; no curves file was produced, so no reference comparison exists for this example.

scope_of_loss.what_was_given_up: The largest and most convincing ground-truth comparison available in this repository: ~12,000 curves from the paper's flagship decryptM Dasatinib TMT phosphoproteome reanalysis, with shipped per-curve reference values for pEC50, Curve F_Value, Curve P_Value, Curve Relevance Score, Curve Fold Change and Curve Regulation.
scope_of_loss.what_remains: Two complete worked examples still provide reference evidence for the same single cli_wrapper module: kinobeads_dasatinib (LFQ protein, 8.2 MiB input, base run plus two deterministic --mad runs) and viability_ctrp_40 (cell viability, 155 KiB input, base run plus two --fdr runs). Both base runs produced curves files for exact comparison against their shipped references.
scope_of_loss.module_still_required: cli_wrapper remains a required module because both remaining active tutorials map to it, so the implementer and the fresh independent verifier are unaffected.
scope_of_loss.honest_limitation: Verification coverage is now narrower than planned. The remaining inputs are 8.2 MiB and 155 KiB, so the wrapper is not exercised against the ~16 MiB / ~12k-curve scale, and no evidence in this run speaks to its behaviour at that size or runtime. This must be stated in USAGE.md rather than implied away.

not_a_defect: This exclusion reflects a container resource limit and an orchestration misjudgement by the coordinator, which launched three multi-core examples concurrently on 4 CPUs instead of queueing them as orchestration.md permits. It is not evidence of any problem in curve_curator, in the shipped example, or in the executor's work.
tutorial_retained_in_state: The decryptm_dasatinib entry stays in reports/agent-runs.json tutorials[] so its source hash continues to be checked; only its required execution assignment is released.
correction_2026_09_26: An earlier revision of this file, and the commit messages that referenced it, stated that 'three concurrent executors each honoured available_cores=5'. That was wrong: the shipped configs request 5 (decryptM), 2 (kinobeads) and 5 (viability). The real figure is ~12 concurrent workers on 4 CPUs, not 15. Corrected here after the kinobeads executor reported its actual value, which was then verified directly against all three shipped tomls. The substance of the exclusion decision is unaffected -- oversubscription was still roughly 3x and the measured load average was ~47 -- but the detail was overstated and is fixed rather than left standing. reports/coordinator-selection-review.md stated this correctly as 'two example configs request available_cores = 5'.
